references.text: Pharaoh's order to Joseph to send wagons to fetch his family, and Joseph's execution of this mission.
Jacob's decision to go to Egypt after seeing the wagons and hearing about Joseph's status.
Jacob sets out and travels to Beersheba where he offers sacrifices to God, the immediate context for the departure in verse 5.
Pharaoh's welcome of Jacob and his family into Egypt.
'My father was a wandering Aramean, and he went down to Egypt' – a summary of Jacob's descent into Egypt.
Direct narrative connection: The preparation of the wagons (45:21) is the immediate cause of their departure on them (46:5).
Direct narrative follow-up: The departure on the wagons (46:5) leads immediately to the presentation before Pharaoh (47:7).
Theological symmetry: The departure to Egypt (46:5) and the return from Egypt (49:25/47:7 context) mark the cycle of God's providence.
